candidates.text: A scheduler should compute target dates for recurring tasks inside a planning horizon and only generate day-candidates for the current planning day, so recurring work spreads across available days instead of piling onto the first day.
candidates.rationale: Story 017 was triggered by Laundry, Meal prep, Grocery, and Clean kitchen all competing on day 1 and cascading forward. The fix replaced an 'every due task is due today' check with horizon-aware target dates, which is the central reusable insight from this story.

candidates.text: When scheduling recurring work of the same priority, prefer more-frequent tasks (e.g., daily) over less-frequent tasks (e.g., weekly) so daily commitments are protected and less-frequent tasks only claim leftover budget or honestly overflow.
candidates.rationale: Story 017 verification required that a daily task never force other tasks to overflow if they can be placed on other days. The review also flagged the need for a focused test proving daily tasks win under budget pressure.
